Exposure within a buffer

Source: R/sep.R
bufexp.Rd

For each receptor (a home, a school), the number of sources (bars, polluting sites, hot spots) within distance r, their summed weights and the distance to the nearest: the buffer measure of exposure assessment. Distances are planar, or great-circle metres when lonlat = TRUE (the coordinates then longitude and latitude in degrees).

Usage

bufexp(x, y = NULL, src, r, w = NULL, lonlat = FALSE)

Arguments

x, y

The points: x and y numeric vectors of equal length; or x a matrix or data frame with columns named x and y (or X and Y, as sf::st_coordinates() names them, or lon and lat with lonlat = TRUE) and y NULL; or x an sf or sfc object of POINT geometries, whose coordinate reference system must agree with lonlat. An unnamed two-column matrix is read as x then y; other columns are never taken by position. Vectors given separately (x, y, and w or t where a function takes them) are matched by name when every one is named and no name repeats, as elsewhere in the package; otherwise by position. No missing or infinite values.

src

The sources: a matrix or data frame of two coordinate columns, as x.

r

The radius: one number from 0, in the unit of the coordinates (metres when lonlat = TRUE).

w

NULL for a weight of 1 per source, or one weight from 0 per source.

lonlat

TRUE when the receptors and sources are longitude and latitude in degrees.

Value

A data frame with one row per receptor: count, wsum and near.

References

Nuckols, J. R., Ward, M. H. and Jarup, L. (2004). Using geographic information systems for exposure assessment in environmental epidemiology studies. Environmental Health Perspectives, 112(9), 1007-1015. doi:10.1289/ehp.6738

See also

Other spatial epidemiology: bayout(), bym2sc(), ecolrg(), evfilt(), kerexp(), lerprc(), sfrail(), spbias(), spsir()

Examples

rec <- cbind(x = c(0, 1, 5), y = c(0, 1, 5))
src <- cbind(x = c(0.5, 4), y = c(0.5, 4))
bufexp(rec, src = src, r = 1.5)
#>   count wsum      near
#> 1     1    1 0.7071068
#> 2     1    1 0.7071068
#> 3     1    1 1.4142136
